hook: Alexey Kurakin built an early research career studying pattern recognition and hand gesture recognition before moving into deep learning. At Google he became one of the first researchers to show that adversarial examples, inputs deliberately perturbed to fool machine learning models, remain effective even after being printed and photographed with a camera, publishing this result with Ian Goodfellow and Samy Bengio as Adversarial Examples in the Physical World. The same period he co-authored Adversarial Machine Learning at Scale, studying how adversarial training could be applied to large image classifiers. In 2016 he demonstrated a physical adversarial attack live at the GeekPwn security conference alongside Ian Goodfellow. He later broadened his research to semi-supervised learning, co-authoring methods including FixMatch, ReMixMatch, and AdaMatch, and continues to work as a research scientist at Google.
